subproblem.title: Constant density ratio implies cone (Simon 7.3.1 proof lines 342–360 and Ch. 6, 2.33)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, n ≥ 1 and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity with ∂C = 0, such that for every integer multiplicity representation R = (M, θ, ξ) of C the varifold v(M, θ) is stationary in ℝ^P (R.IsStationaryAlong univ), and suppose there is θ₀ ∈ ℝ with M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = ω_n·ρⁿ·θ₀ (as unitBallVolume n · ofReal(ρⁿ) · ofReal θ₀) for every ρ > 0. Then C is a cone: η_{0,λ#}C = C for every λ > 0 (IsConeCurrent C, i.e. currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (θ : ℝ), 0 < n → IsIntegerMultiplicity C → BoundaryVanishes C → (∀ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, R.Represents C → R.IsStationaryAlong univ) → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → C.massOn (ball 0 ρ) = unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * ENNReal.ofReal θ) → IsConeCurrent C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: proof of Simon 7.3.1, lines 336–360 (chapter-07.txt: stationarity of V_C (3), the monotonicity formula 3.6 of Ch. 4 giving D^⊥r = 0, x ∧ C⃗ = 0, and Lemma 2.33 of Ch. 6), and Simon Ch. 6, 2.25–2.27 and 2.33 (chapter-06.txt lines 441–470, 557–569); step 6 of the parent proof. Uses the sibling mass_eq_measure (M). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) represent C, μ := μ_R, a := ω_n·max(θ₀, 0) (so the hypothesis reads M_{B_ρ(0)}(C) = aρⁿ), r(y) := |y|; for y ∈ M where T_yM exists, p_y is the orthogonal projection onto T_yM and div_M X(y) = trace(p_y∘DX(y)).
0. The first variation is a genuine Lebesgue integral. For increasing (n−1)-indices J let e^J be the basic (n−1)-covector (for n = 1, e^∅ = 1), and for v ∈ ℝ^P let v^♭ ∧ e^J be the n-covector (u₁,…,uₙ) ↦ Σ_b (−1)^{b−1}⟨v, u_b⟩e^J(u₁,…,û_b,…,uₙ). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ₁,…,τₙ) for an orthonormal frame τ of an n-dimensional subspace Q, then Σ_J ζ(v^♭∧e^J)ζ(w^♭∧e^J) = Σ_{b,b'}(−1)^{b+b'}⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_{b'}⟩Σ_J e^J(τ_{≠b})e^J(τ_{≠b'}) = Σ_b⟨v,τ_b⟩⟨w,τ_b⟩ = ⟨p_Q v, w⟩, because by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_J e^J(τ_{≠b})e^J(τ_{≠b'}) is the determinant of the Gram matrix (⟨τ_i, τ_{i'}⟩)_{i≠b, i'≠b'}, which is 1 if b = b' and 0 otherwise (if b ≠ b', the row of τ_{b'} vanishes). Hence for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M the orthogonal projection p_y onto T_yM = approxTangentPlane n M y (which exists and is unique a.e. by the field `orients` and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) equals Π(ξ(y)), where Π(ζ) is the linear map with ⟨Π(ζ)v, w⟩ = Σ_J ζ(v^♭∧e^J)ζ(w^♭∧e^J), a continuous (quadratic) function of ζ. So y ↦ p_y is a.e. strongly measurable on M, and for a C¹ field X with compact support the function y ↦ θ(y)·trace(p_y∘DX(y)) (= θ·tangentialDivergence n M X) is a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by n·sup‖DX‖·θ·1_{spt X}, which is integrable on M because spt X is a compact set. Thus R.firstVariation X = ∫ div_M X dμ is the integral of an integrable function, and the first-variation hypothesis is a genuine identity of integrals.
1. By M (U = ℝ^P), μ(B_ρ(0)) = aρⁿ for every ρ > 0. As closedBall(0, ρ) = ⋂_{ρ'>ρ} B_{ρ'}(0) and μ(B_{ρ+1}(0)) < ∞, μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) = lim_{ρ'↓ρ} aρ'ⁿ = aρⁿ; and μ({0}) = lim_{ρ↓0} aρⁿ = 0 since n ≥ 1.
2. Stationarity. By hypothesis R.IsStationaryAlong univ: ∫ div_M X dμ = R.firstVariation X = 0 for every C¹ X : ℝ^P → ℝ^P with compact support (the tangency condition X(y) ∈ T_y ℝ^P is vacuous: tangentSpace univ y contains every v, via γ(t) = y + tv), the integral being genuine by step 0.
3. Monotonicity identity (Ch. 4, 3.1–3.6 with ξ = 0, R = ∞, H = 0). For ε ∈ (0, 1) let φ_ε be as in Ch. 4, 3.5 (C¹, nonincreasing, = 1 on (−∞, 1], = 0 on [1 + ε, ∞)). Testing step 2 with X(y) = φ_ε(r/ρ)y gives, exactly as in Ch. 4, 3.2–3.4, d/dρ(ρ^{−n}I(ρ)) = ρ^{−n}J'(ρ) with I(ρ) = ∫φ_ε(r/ρ) dμ, J(ρ) = ∫φ_ε(r/ρ)|D^⊥r|² dμ, D^⊥r(y) := (Id − p_y)(y/|y|) for y ≠ 0 (I, J are C¹ by differentiation under the integral sign; the point 0 is μ-null by step 1). Integrating from σ to ρ and using that ∂_tφ_ε(r/t) ≥ 0 is supported in {r/(1+ε) ≤ t ≤ r}, where t^{−n} lies between r^{−n} and (1+ε)ⁿr^{−n}, gives Ch. 4, 3.5: ∫ r^{−n}(φ_ε(r/ρ) − φ_ε(r/σ))|D^⊥r|² dμ ≤ ρ^{−n}I(ρ) − σ^{−n}I(σ) ≤ (1+ε)ⁿ∫ r^{−n}(φ_ε(r/ρ) − φ_ε(r/σ))|D^⊥r|² dμ (the integrands vanish where r ≤ σ, so r^{−n} ≤ σ^{−n} on their supports). Letting ε ↓ 0 (dominated convergence) yields Ch. 4, 3.6: for 0 < σ < ρ, ρ^{−n}μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) − σ^{−n}μ(closedBall(0, σ)) = ∫_{closedBall(0,ρ) ∖ closedBall(0,σ)} |D^⊥r|²r^{−n} dμ.
4. By step 1 the left side of 3.6 is a − a = 0. Hence |D^⊥r|²r^{−n} = 0 μ-a.e. on every annulus closedBall(0, ρ) ∖ closedBall(0, σ), so D^⊥r = 0 μ-a.e. on ℝ^P ∖ {0} (countable union of annuli), and μ-a.e. on ℝ^P as μ({0}) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, this means: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M, y ∈ T_yM.
5. "x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e." For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M, ξ(y)(α) = ±α(τ₁, …, τₙ) with τ an orthonormal basis of T_yM (field `orients`) and y ∈ T_yM (step 4). Then for every (n+1)-covector β, writing (ι_yβ)(v₁, …, vₙ) := β(y, v₁, …, vₙ), we get ξ(y)(ι_yβ) = ±β(y, τ₁, …, τₙ) = 0, because y is a linear combination of τ₁, …, τₙ and β is alternating.
6. Lemma 2.33 (homotopy formula for h(t, y) = tλ⁻¹y + (1 − t)y, made explicit). Fix λ > 0 and ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), and let R_ω > 0 with tsupport ω ⊆ closedBall(0, R_ω). For s ∈ [0, 1] let c(s) := 1 + s(λ⁻¹ − 1), which lies between 1 and λ⁻¹, so c(s) ≥ m := min(1, λ⁻¹) > 0; let h_s(y) := c(s)y (h₀ = Id, h₁ = η_{0,λ}), β_s := h_s^#ω, i.e. β_s(y)(v) = c(s)ⁿω(c(s)y)(v), and F(s) := C(β_s) = ∫_M θ ξ(β_s) dHⁿ. Let X(y) := y and L_X the Lie derivative, (L_Xβ)(y) = nβ(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for an n-form β. Differentiating β_s(y) = c(s)ⁿω(c(s)y) gives ∂_sβ_s = (c'(s)/c(s))·L_X(β_s). For s ∈ [0, 1] the forms β_s and ∂_sβ_s are smooth, supported in closedBall(0, R_ω/m) (tsupport β_s = c(s)⁻¹·tsupport ω), and uniformly bounded together with their first derivatives; since ∫_{M ∩ closedBall(0,R_ω/m)} θ dHⁿ < ∞, dominated convergence shows F is differentiable with F'(s) = (c'(s)/c(s))·C(L_Xβ_s). By Cartan's formula L_Xβ_s = d(ι_Xβ_s) + ι_X dβ_s, where ι_Xβ_s ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(ℝ^P) (smooth, compactly supported). Hence C(L_Xβ_s) = ∂C(ι_Xβ_s) + C(ι_X dβ_s). The first term is 0 since ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C, n ≥ 1). The second is ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(ι_y(dβ_s(y))) dHⁿ(y) = 0 by step 5. So F' ≡ 0 on [0, 1] and C(η_{0,λ}^#ω) = F(1) = F(0) = C(ω).
7. IsConeCurrent. For λ > 0, dilation 0 λ is surjective, so dilation 0 λ '' ℝ^P = ℝ^P ⊇ tsupport ω and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = (blowUp C 0 λ)(ω) = C(η_{0,λ}^#ω), where (η_{0,λ}^#ω)(y) = ω(λ⁻¹y)∘(λ⁻¹·) = β₁(y) (affinePushforward with L = λ⁻¹Id, b = −λ⁻¹·0 = 0). By step 6 this equals C(ω). Hence IsConeCurrent C.
proof_key_steps: mass_eq_measure turns the hypothesis into μ_C(B_ρ(0)) = aρⁿ for all ρ, hence for closed balls, and μ_C({0}) = 0.
The stationary monotonicity identity (Simon 4.3.6) forces D^⊥r = 0 μ_C-a.e., i.e. y ∈ T_yM for a.e. y, so ξ(y)(ι_yβ) = 0 (x ∧ C⃗ = 0).
Homotopy formula for y ↦ c(s)y (Lemma 6.2.33): d/ds C(h_s^#ω) = (c'/c)[∂C(ι_Xβ_s) + C(ι_X dβ_s)] = 0, so η_{0,λ#}C = C.
Translate η_{0,λ#}C = C into IsConeCurrent via currentEval and dilation 0 λ '' ℝ^P = ℝ^P.
